inventory.observation: One shared Cartesian frame: horizontal x axis and vertical y axis intersect at the lower-left origin. The x axis extends left of the origin and beyond b on the right; the y axis extends below the origin and high above the plotted region. Positive x is right, positive y is up. Direction arrowheads are visible along the positive axes.

Italic x is below the right end; italic y is left of the upper vertical axis. An oval origin glyph appears below-left of the intersection; pixels alone do not distinguish letter O from numeral 0 with sufficient confidence.

A small arrow-over-i-like glyph is below the positive horizontal axis between origin and a. A small arrow-over-j-like glyph is left of the positive vertical axis. These are distinct from the axis direction arrows. Exact typographic basis-glyph family is not independently certain.

A single thick solid increasing, concave-down upper graph runs through the tops of the two vertical boundaries. It has a substantial solid exterior piece to the left of a and another solid exterior piece to the right of b. Both terminate without a deliberately isolated endpoint marker. No dashed graph section is visible.
The label y=f(x) sits above the graph toward its middle-right. No leader for this label is visible.

Two solid vertical boundaries rise from the x axis to the graph: left boundary above a, right boundary above b. Their tops lie on the same graph, and a is positive with b to its right. Italic a and b sit below their respective axis feet. There are no numeric ticks or values.

The curvilinear region bounded by the x axis, those two verticals, and the graph is diagonally hatched, with strokes sloping down-right. Hatching stays between a and b; no exterior graph piece is hatched. There is no area or answer formula inside the region.

Defining intersections are origin, a-axis foot, b-axis foot, and graph/boundary top intersections. The original does not visibly assign separate names or isolated dot markers to the four boundary corners.

sourceModernizationBoundary: Exact drawing regularization, semantic colors, English captions and larger labels may be modern additions; they cannot omit either exterior curve piece or the hatching and shared frame.
